title: Intent's own estate never received the 3.1.0 post-pull hook carriers the trawl gave every other estate
body:
Intent's own estate never received the post-pull carriers the 3.1.0 canon installs, and the release found out.

**Seen 2026-09-19** at the 3.1.0 cut: the driver's canon regeneration (`claude upgrade --apply`) wrote `.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` and their `.intent` shims as new files and refused to fold them into the release commit, correctly. Every other estate got these hooks in the fleet trawl of 2026-09-18; Intent's own repository, whose hooks live in the tracked `.githooks/` reached by `core.hooksPath`, did not. They were landed by hand at 3d778acf4 with the shims ignored like `pre-commit.intent`.

**The ask:** find why the trawl's Intent run did not converge its own `.githooks/` (the kit's step 3 runs `claude upgrade --apply --skip-settings` on the other estates), and whether a self-hosted tree needs its own line in the kit or in `claude upgrade`. S.


CLOSED 2026-09-19, on vc's ruling, by the record rather than a change: the kit never ran on Intent. Intent's own estate was brought up by e06e94d2b (`intent sync --apply`, then `intent upgrade`) and d58ce1593 (`intent organize`), and neither runs `intent claude upgrade --apply`, the one step that installs the post-pull carriers. The kit (`refs/bank/dc/trawl/trawl-estate.sh`) runs that step, and canon.rs `hooks_dir` resolves the hooks directory through `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which follows `core.hooksPath`. So a tracked hooks dir is already handled: Gtools (`.githooks`) and Laksa (`bin/hooks`) received all three carriers in the trawl and track their `.intent` shims as they track `pre-commit.intent`. Intent, which ignores its shims, got them by hand at 3d778acf4. A self-hosted tree needs no line of its own, only to go through `claude upgrade --apply` like any other estate.
